meta.scope: Yemen Batch 5 — Territorial control dynamics densification: IRG, Ansar Allah, and fragmented control framing under severe conflict constraints.

candidates.title: Internationally Recognized Government territorial control framing
candidates.publisher: Derived from monitoring and reporting sources
candidates.description: Framing of territorial control by the internationally recognized government and affiliated forces. Recent shifts have expanded IRG-affiliated control over large shares of southern and eastern territory (including Hadramawt and Al Maharah in recent reporting), though population centres and economic weight remain contested.
candidates.notes: Primary IRG control densification. Fluid and contested.

candidates.title: Ansar Allah territorial control framing
candidates.publisher: Derived from monitoring and reporting sources
candidates.description: Framing of territorial control by Ansar Allah (Houthis). Control is concentrated in northern highlands and includes Sana’a and a large share of the population; a parallel administrative, fiscal and monetary system operates in these areas.
candidates.notes: Primary Ansar Allah control densification. Population-weighted importance is high.

candidates.title: Territorial fragmentation and dual-authority framing
candidates.description: System-level framing of Yemen’s fragmented territorial and institutional landscape: dual monetary systems, dual fiscal capacities, contested ports and oil infrastructure, and multiple armed actors. Continuously cited in every macro, humanitarian and external analysis.
referenced_by: All dual-rate, fiscal and humanitarian nodes
candidates.notes: Highest-centrality structural frame for the entire Yemen graph. Underpins dual FX, dual fiscal and humanitarian patterns.
